questions.explanation: CO = SV × HR. Stroke volume is EDV − ESV. On echo it can also be found with LVOT area × LVOT VTI.

questions.stem: An LVOT diameter of 2.0 cm and an LVOT VTI of 20 cm give a stroke volume of approximately:
questions.explanation: LVOT area = 0.785 × D² = 0.785 × 4 = 3.14 cm². SV = 3.14 cm² × 20 cm ≈ 63 mL.

questions.stem: According to the Frank-Starling mechanism, increasing preload (within physiologic limits) will:
questions.explanation: More stretch of the myocardial fibers at end-diastole (preload) produces a stronger contraction, so stroke volume increases. This holds until the fibers are overstretched.
